reason: ImageGlass already shows my screenshots and PNGs fine and I know where everything is. Speed numbers on a developer's own PC don't mean much to me, and I'm not relearning a viewer from one person's 0.4.1.
why_switch_or_not: I might unzip the portable version out of curiosity since it's free and needs no admin rights, and flip through a screenshot folder once or twice. But most of that feature list (RAW, PSD, 3D models, an editor, a scanner importer) is stuff I never use, and it makes the app sound bigger than I need. I'd go back to ImageGlass because I'd also have to re-tick the file formats in Windows Settings, and it isn't open source like ImageGlass.
current_app_pros: ImageGlass looks clean and modern, it's open source, and it opens my PNG screenshots and phone photos without any fuss. I know its keys and menus by heart.
current_app_pains: Nothing much. It's a little slow when I hold down the arrow key through a few hundred screenshots, but not enough to make me change.
objection: It's one developer's 0.4.1. I don't know if it will still be updated in two years, and I don't want to retrain my fingers and reset my default apps for something that might disappear.
would_change_my_mind: Seeing it stay maintained for a year or two, with the source open like ImageGlass, and a plain mode that hides the editor, gallery and everything else so it feels like a simple fast viewer for screenshots.
